sources.title: Arch540_2026 B_testfit: PROMPTS.md and complete/ files (CLAUDE.md, brief, check.py, rules, lot, .claude/)
sources.extract: PROMPTS.md: lay out buildings for maximum floor area within the rules, then draw the plan; variants add checker, skill, reviewer, hook (step 5 tries to write a developer scheme unchanged), with/without-skill comparison. complete/ holds CLAUDE.md, brief.md, check.py, layout_format.md, lot.json, rules.md, output/, work/, .claude/ (agents, hooks, skills/site-layout, settings.json). rules.md: 3 m setback; sun gap at least 0.7 x southern height where east-west extents overlap; 12 m spacing; 40 m max height with storey ranges; at least 25% unbuilt. check.py: Shapely checker, PASS/FAIL per rule, total GFA and open-space %, exit codes 0/1/2; limits: simplified sun-gap test, axis-aligned rectangles, hard-coded thresholds, GFA = footprint x storeys with no core deduction. brief.md: 2D residential test-fit; tower 18x18 m 8-12 storeys, slab 40x12 m 4-8, short 24x12 m 4-8; 3.2 m storeys; deliverables layout.json, plan.png, message naming the binding rule.

sources.title: Arch540_2026 agents_notes.html (session 4 notes, demos B, C, D)
sources.extract: B_testfit: lot 5,276 m2 (about 90 x 70 m); B1 same prompt gave 16,272 / 13,968 / 15,552 m2; B4 reviewer APPROVE (R1-R5 PASS, both runs); B5 hook gate.py blocked a layout (R2 FAIL, gap 12.0 m, needs 26.9 m), never fired in 7 normal runs, and a hook watching the file tool missed the command line; B6 skill changed method (scheme gallery 3 of 3 vs 0 of 3), not floor area. C_design_space: 80 x 60 m Vancouver lot (49.25 N), goals GFA, winter sun (21 Dec 9:00-15:00, max 6.0 h), shape factor; C0 grid search 7,308 combos, 3,680 valid, 8 on the front; C2 no scorer 50 of 75 valid vs scorer 61 of 75; C3 one run imported the scoring functions so evaluations were never counted; C5 six helpers, main context near 50k tokens; 'Tested (one run, 6 minutes)' note on the complete project: six helpers, 300 evaluations, then the scoring script refused more; rows 82, north-high-south-low 80, terraced 18 (three of six helpers; others not given); Step 5 (steps/ folder): 329 evaluations in total against about 40 each (about 240) asked; the page does not reconcile 329 with the 300 cap; C6 impossible target stopped after 5 (no hook) or 7 (hook) evaluations. D_team: 100 x 70 m block, FSR 2.8, 220-280 homes; hidden contradiction (CEO wants 250+ homes, FSR allows about 239) caught by the constraints helper in 3 of 3 runs; three runs, three schemes (237, 222, 226 homes); D3 (one run, no constraints helper): a designer estimated about 255 homes, the tool measured 223; round 1 4 of 12 schemes failed (3 play-area sun, 1 park shadow), round 2 12 of 12 passed; the bullets sit under the three-runs heading and 12 = 4 designers x 3 runs, but the page does not say 'across three runs' outright. Lessons: checks in code hold where requests do not; a guard covers only the path it watches; measure rather than estimate; run several times.

sources.extract: 12 FAQs. Policy dates to 1997, last updated 2011; only minor changes to upper limits in three decades. Phase 1 closed; Phase 2 draft options early 2027; recommendations to Council in 2027. The Vancouver Tall Challenge (Buildner with the City and UBC SALA, to 30 Nov 2026) 'will not determine the policy'. Bay Parkade FAQ: buildings up to 600 ft (183 m) may be considered in the current policy area; the proposed towers of about 783, 889 and 1,034 ft exceed it. Protected views and whether entries are binding are not addressed.

flags.detail: Opened UpCodes pages do not list jurisdictions or pricing (S28). Confirm coverage or use City of Vancouver primary documents.

flags.detail: Pages mention Australian clients only. The Core plan lists 3D modelling (S33) and the education page's studio framework includes massing and constraints (S50), so 3D modelling is stated; Canada or Vancouver data coverage is not stated on any opened page.

Floor plates (1,500 / 2,000 / 2,500 m2) and 4.0 m floor-to-floor are editable placeholders, not sourced. flags.claim: The cove.tool SaaS is not described anywhere on the cove.inc pages, and its availability cannot be confirmed (round-0 case study and UNRESOLVED flag)
flags.detail: Why false: the cove.inc footer links were never opened. https://cove.inc/analysis-client-support/ is a client hub for analysis.tool, cove's platform, with login, Assembly Builder and operational and embodied carbon tools; https://cove.inc/education-resources/ says no new educational licences after 1 Oct 2025, active access ended 31 Dec 2025, and no replacement (S47). The rename cove.tool to analysis.tool is an inference.

flags.claim: Speckle's free plan caps at 3 users, so a 4-person VTC team would exceed it and must pay
flags.detail: Why false: the Speckle pricing page states Speckle is free for students and educators and /academia offers educational institutions a free workspace by email application (S15, S49). The Explore plan also has a 100-version cap, omitted in round 0. Terms of the academic workspace are not stated.
flags.correction: For a UBC team, apply to academia@speckle.systems; Explore limits are 1 project, 3 users including external collaborators, 100 versions and 30-day history. Treat academic terms as UNVERIFIED until UBC applies. The earlier note that a 4-person team must pay is withdrawn.

flags.claim: Giraffe has no education pricing, and its free-plan and education terms are unconfirmed
flags.detail: Why false: https://www.giraffe.build/universities-and-education (S50) says Giraffe provides free licences to students and universities, with no trial expiry and no credit card, and describes a semester studio framework. The page does not name covered regions.
flags.correction: Giraffe is free for students and universities (vendor statement). Vancouver data coverage remains UNVERIFIED.

flags.claim: In the B_testfit demo, hand estimates were wrong (255 vs 223 homes measured) and the guard was bypassed by a counter import
flags.detail: Why false: agents_notes.html (S09) places 255 vs 223 in demo D step 3 (no constraints helper) and the scoring-function import that escaped the evaluation counter in demo C step 3. B_testfit's own evidence is the three runs (16,272 / 13,968 / 15,552 m2), reviewer APPROVE, and the gate.py block (R2 gap 12.0 m, needs 26.9 m); its B5 hook also missed the command-line path.
flags.correction: Attribute 255 vs 223 to D, the import bypass to C, and keep the B evidence to B. The case study is split into B, C and D.

flags.claim: Ladybug licence: 'copyleft either way', so the difference between AGPL and GPL does not matter
flags.detail: Why false: the ladybug core LICENSE is GNU Affero GPL v3, as are ladybug-grasshopper and honeybee-radiance; Butterfly is GPL-3.0+ (S20). AGPL section 13 adds a network-interaction duty that GPL v3 lacks: a modified version must offer its source to users interacting with it remotely. Whether calling the libraries unmodified, or as a separate process, triggers it is a legal question not settled here.
flags.correction: Record the core libraries as AGPL-3.0. Decision for the DATA packet (not legal advice): run ladybug/honeybee client-side or in a separately licensed service, or license the platform (or that service) so its source can be offered. Hosting modified Ladybug code means publishing it.

flags.claim: TestFit does not show tall mixed-use buildings (it is only parking, multi-family and similar)
flags.detail: Why false: the TestFit pricing FAQ (S10) says Site Solver provides detailed typology solutions suitable for mixed-use developments. The typology list still omits office, high-rise and tower, and the MCP page (S12) names no building types. /solutions/universities (S51) exists for schools; the /universities path 404s.
flags.correction: Mixed-use is claimed for Site Solver only (from USD 15,000/yr). Office and tower capability are unverified. A university route exists with unknown terms.

flags.claim: Archistar's current product line is plan review only; no design generation is described (round-0 case study and S27 extract)
flags.detail: Why false: the Industry & Certifiers page (S52) advertises a 3D Generative design library surfacing 1000's of compliant designs and a NEW and FREE Autodesk Forma integration with sunlight, wind and noise analysis. Vendor claims; no terms, no Vancouver rule set, no tower capability; the products page (S27) still lists only AI PreCheck.
flags.correction: Describe Archistar as AI plan review (AI PreCheck) plus an advertised generative-design library and Forma integration whose capability is unverified.

flags.claim: Protected-view rules: the Public Views Guidelines (Council-approved 10 July 2024; replaced the 1989 View Protection Guidelines) and the Higher Buildings Policy govern permissible tower heights downtown, and the QE Park skyline view is checked against them
flags.detail: The City dataset (S54) says development in its 24 polygons is limited in height but has no height field, names neither document and says the authoritative source is the City's bylaws. The Guidelines PDF and Council papers (S69), the QE Park page (S63) and the 1997 policy (S62) returned 403 or no text. Shape Your City says protected views are outside the review (S71). S75: the current policy area may consider up to 600 ft (183 m), below the 244-305 m (800-1,000 ft) in S78. Heights, and whether the VTC block lies in a cone, stay UNVERIFIED until a person opens the PDF (A5).

flags.claim: Education or student access for TestFit and Finch (Forma and Snaptrude resolved in r2)
flags.detail: TestFit /solutions/universities invites class enrolment, terms not stated; the footer For Students link goes to the same page (S51). Finch: no education offer on the pricing page (S37). Negative or partial results, not proof of absence.

flags.claim: Terms of Speckle's free academic workspace
flags.detail: The academia page (S49) lists no eligibility criteria, limits, competition-use wording or terms. Whether it applies to a student competition team, lifts the 3-user and 100-version caps, or keeps the 30-day history limit is unknown until UBC applies (A11).

flags.claim: Licence decision for the open-source platform: AGPL (Ladybug, Honeybee) vs Apache-2.0 (Speckle server, specklepy) vs MIT (Hypar Elements, HyparSpace) vs GPL-3.0+ (Butterfly)
flags.detail: Not decided in this packet. Handed to the DATA packet: choose the platform licence and deployment boundary (client-side, separate service, or AGPL-compatible whole) before any CLIM or ENER module bundles Ladybug code. Apache-2.0 and MIT components can be combined into an AGPL or GPL-3.0 whole in one direction only; confirm with a licence review.

flags.claim: 'Rhino + Grasshopper + Ladybug is the dominant competition modelling stack' and 'Butterfly is the wind route'
flags.detail: No source for dominant; relabelled a team assumption. Butterfly plugin dates from March 2017 with no stated maintenance (S18). Eddy3D (S74, opened r3) is the maintained Rhino/Grasshopper wind route found: free for all users (vendor statement), OpenFOAM, active releases, Rhino 8.27; plugin licence not named, validity for towers not stated. SimScale has no free wind route (see r3 flags); Infrared and Forma wind are candidates, not recommendations.

flags.claim: Autodesk Forma access for a VTC student team is UNKNOWN, and its analyses (sun, wind, noise, carbon) can only be stated as uncitable general knowledge
flags.detail: Why false: Autodesk's Forma blog (S64, 1 Nov 2024) says students and educators get Forma free and names the sun study, noise, wind and embodied carbon. The education page is 403 (S43), so seat terms are second-hand (free named-user seat, renewable 1-year, school email).
flags.correction: Forma is free for students and educators (vendor statement); a logged-in team member confirms eligibility. Sun, noise, wind and embodied carbon are vendor-stated; daylight, microclimate and supertall validity stay UNVERIFIED. Forma Site Design name and 30-day trial are seen only in search results.

flags.claim: Snaptrude has no student or education offer; a 4-person team needs four free single-user accounts or a paid plan
flags.detail: Why false: snaptrude.com/students and the blog (S66, S67; 13 Nov 2025, updated 22 Jun 2026) describe a free Student Plan. The /education 404 was the wrong URL, and the pricing page does not link /students (S36).
flags.correction: Free for enrolled architecture, design and engineering students and educators: full features, unlimited projects, real-time collaboration, 120 AI credits a year (S66), 1-year renewable licence verified by school email, educational use only. Whether that covers a prize competition is UNVERIFIED.

flags.claim: Vancouver's View Protection Guidelines (with the Higher Buildings Policy) govern the protected-view envelope for the VTC tower (steps 0, 1b, 7b and the UNVERIFIED flag)
flags.detail: Why false: on 10 July 2024 Council repealed the 1989 View Protection Guidelines and approved Public Views Guidelines, removing 14 and amending 11 of 38 views (search snippets of Council papers, S69, 403, second-hand). Shape Your City (S71, opened) says protected views are not reviewed in the Higher Buildings work. The 24-record dataset (S54) fits 38 minus 14 (inference).
flags.correction: Steps 0, 1b, 7b and flags now name the Public Views Guidelines (2024, replaced the 1989 VPG). Height rules stay UNVERIFIED until a person opens the PDF.

flags.claim: SimScale has no academic or student plan (S58 case study)
flags.detail: Why false: simscale.com/academic-program/ (S68) lists a Free Academic Plan (1,000 core hours, private projects, advanced solvers such as PWC excluded; thesis students 12 months) and an Academic Sponsorship Plan for student design-competition teams (no terms or application steps shown).
flags.correction: Routes: Community (free; private projects not included, so projects are implied public) or Academic Sponsorship Plan by application (terms and turnaround unknown). Public projects may expose the scheme before anonymous judging.

flags.claim: (r1 critique) Infrared.city's 'Students & small studies' label belongs to the Starter tier, not the Free tier
flags.detail: Why false: re-read on 21 Oct 2026 by the r2 reviser and the r2 critic; the label sits on the Free tier and Starter is labelled small sites (S31).
flags.correction: Free tier: students and small studies, 900 one-time tokens, 42-day expiry. S31 extract kept; the UNRESOLVED flag is closed.

flags.claim: Snaptrude's educational-use-only Student Plan covers an entry to a competition that carries prize money
flags.detail: The Student Plan is educational use only (coursework, studio projects, portfolios; commercial or freelance work needs a professional licence, S66); the blog states no restriction (S67). The VTC carries CAD 15,000 in prizes (S71, S01). Ask Snaptrude (communications@snaptrude.com) before relying on the plan (A8); see the all-licences flag below.

flags.claim: Facts known only from second-hand search results, not opened
flags.detail: Council 10 July 2024 decision and numbers (14 of 38 views removed, 11 amended); City statement that the 2024 views will be maintained; UNDRIP Strategy details (adopted 25 Oct 2022, 79 calls to action, Action Plan endorsed 25 Jun 2024); Autodesk education-page terms; Forma Site Design 30-day trial. All sources 403 or unreachable in r3 (S43, S69, S70, S72); a person must open each before the team cites it (A5, A6, A7).

flags.claim: Cloud tools keep the competition model private until judging
flags.detail: SimScale Community projects are implied public (S58, S68); Speckle has public links (S15); Giraffe offers view-only sharing (S33); Snaptrude shares workspaces (S66). Any of these could expose the scheme before anonymous judging. Check each tool's default visibility and sharing settings before uploading the entry model (A13).

flags.claim: Board count, size and the 10 MB limit used in the step 8 and 9 pre-flight checks come from the competition page (S01)
flags.detail: Re-read 21 Oct 2026 (r3): S01 states English-only submission, anonymous judging and the deadline. It does not state boards, sheet size, file size, tower heights, FSR, jury criteria or submission contents; those figures come from the project description (S78) and are unverified against the brief (S77, not opened).
flags.correction: Steps 0, 8 and 9 now cite S01 only for English, anonymity, dates, fees and prizes, and cite 4 x A2, 10 MB, 9.0 FSR, 244-305 m and jury weights to S78 as 'project description, unverified'.

flags.claim: SimScale Community or the Free Academic Plan is a usable CFD route for the wind study ('a real CFD route if a surrogate is not trusted'; 'usable before 30 Nov: yes for basic CFD on Community')
flags.detail: S68 excludes LBM, PWC, Multi-purpose, Electromagnetics, SPH and Marc from the Free Academic Plan; S58 shows Community incompressible flow only as 'Limited' and LBM and PWC as add-ons on Professional and Enterprise only. LBM as the solver behind PWC is an inference.
flags.correction: SimScale case study and step 4 rewritten: no urban-wind route on Community or Free Academic; at most limited steady incompressible CFD with CFD skill. The 'real CFD route' wording is withdrawn.

flags.claim: (r3 critique) The Academic Sponsorship Plan is the only route to SimScale urban wind (pedestrian wind comfort and LBM)
flags.detail: The student-competitions page (S76, opened r3) says sponsored teams get 3,000 core hours and private projects with all simulation types except Multi-purpose, Incompressible (LBM) and Pedestrian Wind Comfort. Sponsorship therefore excludes the same urban-wind analyses.
flags.correction: No free SimScale route to LBM or PWC exists on any plan page opened (S58, S68, S76); they need a paid Professional or Enterprise add-on (price not listed). Sponsorship gives other CFD types with private projects, by application. Access for tower wind is set to 'no free route', not 'unknown pending sponsorship'.

flags.claim: (r3 critique) The course notes state the demo D round counts (4 of 12 failed, 12 of 12 passed) as across three runs, so 'inferred' can be dropped
flags.detail: Re-read r3 (S09): 'In round 1, 4 of 12 schemes failed a hard rule (3 on play-area sun, 1 on park shadow). In round 2, 12 of 12 passed.' The bullets sit under the three-runs heading and 12 = 4 designers x 3 runs, but the page does not say 'across three runs'. The 255 vs 223 estimate (D3) is one run.
flags.correction: Counts kept as 'read as totals across 3 runs (not stated outright)'; D3 marked n=1 (accepted).

flags.claim: (r3 critique) Demo C5 used 329 evaluations against a 300 budget in the complete project
flags.detail: S09: 329 evaluations in total is the Step 5 (steps/ folder) result against about 40 each (about 240) asked; the 300 cap belongs to the complete project's one-run, 6-minute test (six helpers, 300 evaluations, then the script refused more; rows 82, north-high-south-low 80, terraced 18). The page does not reconcile the two.
flags.correction: Case study C reports the two results separately; no single 329-versus-300 comparison is made.

flags.claim: Every education or academic licence the plan relies on may be used for an entry to a competition with CAD 15,000 in prizes (Forma, Giraffe, ShapeDiver, Speckle academia, SimScale academic, Snaptrude, Infrared Free)
flags.detail: Forma terms unread (403, S43). Snaptrude: educational use only (S66). ShapeDiver academic: non-commercial use only (S39). Giraffe: EULA lists only Core, Teams, Enterprise and does not address education, commercial use or competitions (S33). Speckle: no terms (S49). SimScale: Sponsorship is aimed at competition teams (S76), Free Academic terms not stated. Infrared: not stated. Rhino buy page states no use restriction (EULA unread, S25). Eddy3D: free for all users stated (S74).
flags.correction: No tool is confirmed in writing. Ask the Q&A (A3) and each vendor (A8); the summary in notes lists status per tool. Until then plan the entry model so it can be rebuilt without an educational-only tool.

flags.claim: The VTC brief, site plans and 3D model have never been opened
flags.detail: S01's 'Download brief' is '#' and the language and site-file links have no href in the fetched text (r3); the City pages do not link the brief (S71, S75). Brief-derived items in the workflow (recommended deliverables, site edges, secondary transit entrance, 'documents are academic, not legal', 'justified breaches may be rewarded', skyline view from QE Park) have no citable source and are tagged brief-unopened. Registration closes 29 Oct (8 days).
flags.correction: Action A1: a team member registers, opens the brief and site files, records page numbers and site coordinates, and the packet re-cites every tagged item. Until then those items are hypotheses, not requirements.

flags.claim: Cone intersection for the VTC site: the block is not georeferenced, so the check could not be run; indicative sample only
flags.detail: Explore API test (r3, S54): intersects() returns cones for a POINT and for a POLYGON. Six approximate downtown station-area points (my own coordinates from memory, not surveyed, not the VTC site) each fell in at least one polygon: Granville (-123.1163, 49.2832) 3.2.3; Burrard (-123.1203, 49.2857) 3.2.2 and B2; City Centre (-123.1186, 49.2823) 3.2.2; Waterfront (-123.1114, 49.2858) 3.2.3 and 9.2; Stadium-Chinatown (-123.1097, 49.2795) 3.2.3 and 9.2; Yaletown-Roundhouse (-123.1218, 49.2746) D and 3.2.1.
flags.correction: Expect protected-view constraints on a downtown block (inference from six points). Run the query for the block corners and centre after A1 (action A4); heights still need the Guidelines PDF (A5).

flags.claim: Fee per category and student registration mechanics
flags.detail: S01 lists EUR 140 and EUR 120 under Architect/Enthusiast/Company and Student; the pairing is inferred from list order. Instalment amounts not shown. Student rates need university staff to apply; beebreeders.com/competition-registration-types returned HTTP 521 (r3).
flags.correction: Action A2: a logged-in member confirms the fee per category and starts the student-rate request through university staff before 29 Oct.

flags.claim: Eddy3D is valid and fast enough for a 244-305 m tower in a downtown context, and its plugin licence permits student competition use
flags.detail: S74: free for all users (vendor statement), OpenFOAM and urbanMicroclimateFoam, Rhino 8.27, active releases; no plugin licence name, height or domain limits, validation or run times stated. Needs a container engine (Docker or Podman) or BlueCFD-Core.
flags.correction: Action A9: test on a simple massing, record set-up and run time, compare with a known case before relying on it. Treat as a candidate, not a recommendation.

unresolved_relationships: How much time each as-is step takes for a 2-4 person team: interview n=0 as of 21 Oct 2026; two 15-minute interviews planned by 5 Nov (A12). Until recorded, no step ranking may drive module priority.
Whether the VTC brief matches the project description (heights 244-305 m, 9.0 FSR, jury weights, four A2 boards, 10 MB, site and transit link): the brief has not been opened (A1).
Causal effect of the number of massing options tested on final design quality or jury score (no sourced relationship).
Whether any commercial tool's built-in thresholds (TestFit, Forma, Infrared, Archistar) match Vancouver policy or VTC criteria (vendors do not expose them).
How Infrared.city surrogate accuracy changes with building height above about 200 m (no sourced figure).

How much a Claude Code agent's run-to-run variation (13,968 to 16,272 m2 in demo B; three different schemes in demo D) carries over to supertall massing; the demos are 40-45 m housing and mixed-use toys.

Required non-residential area (about 103,200 m2 at 9.0 FSR on the full block, basis unconfirmed) -> number of office floors -> share of the 244-305 m height and core size: only N = area / floor plate and height = N x floor-to-floor are known; plate sizes and floor-to-floor heights have no sourced value.

Which of Vancouver's 24 protected view cones (including QE Park 3.2.1-3.2.4) intersect the VTC block and what height each permits under the Public Views Guidelines (2024): the block is not georeferenced (A1, A4), the polygons carry no height and the PDF returned 403 (A5). Six approximate downtown sample points each fall in at least one cone.
Whether the 24-record view-cones dataset equals the 2024 Public Views Guidelines set (38 minus 14 removed is an inference from second-hand figures).

Whether the 1997 Higher Buildings Policy is the policy the VTC brief names (the City page lists it; the brief was not opened), and how the jury treats towers of 244-305 m against the 600 ft (183 m) figure in the current policy area (S75).
Whether Speckle's academic workspace lifts the Explore caps (3 users, 100 versions, 30-day history), which matter for a 4-person team working 40 days.
Whether UBC SALA already holds Rhino lab licences (USD 975 for 30 users), Autodesk education access or a TestFit class agreement (no source; ask the instructor, A10).

Whether Forma's student seat terms (eligibility, renewal, educational-use wording, competition use) apply to a VTC team, and whether its sun, wind and noise criteria are auditable and valid for 244-305 m towers.
Whether any education or academic licence (Forma, Giraffe, ShapeDiver, Speckle, SimScale, Snaptrude, Infrared) may be used for a prize-money competition entry; none confirmed in writing (A3, A8).

Whether any free route to urban wind CFD exists on SimScale (none on S58, S68, S76) and whether Eddy3D (OpenFOAM, free for all users per S74) or the Infrared surrogate is adequate for a 244-305 m tower context (no sourced validity range; Eddy3D run time unmeasured, A9).
Whether SimScale's Academic Sponsorship Plan is open to VTC teams and how fast it is granted; whether Community or other cloud-tool projects are public by default and would break anonymity (A13).
Legal effect of AGPL-3.0 section 13 on a hosted platform that calls or wraps ladybug/honeybee unmodified (needs a licence review; handed to the DATA packet).
Token cost of Infrared solar, UTCI and daylight analyses (only standard 10 and pedestrian wind 50 are listed), hence how many full option sweeps the free 900 tokens allow.
Fee category mapping (EUR 120 and EUR 140), instalment amounts and the student-registration mechanics (S01; beebreeders page HTTP 521) (A2).
Whether Giraffe's student licence maps to a plan in its EULA (EULA lists Core, Teams, Enterprise only) and what data and sharing terms apply.

notes:
Method: claims come from pages opened on 21 Oct 2026 (rounds 0 to r3) unless labelled UNVERIFIED, second-hand, brief-unopened or team assumption. Prices are as shown that day in the vendor's currency. Page text came through a summarising fetch tool. Web search was unavailable in r3, so second-hand items (S43, S62, S63, S69, S70, S72) stay opened:false. The actions table lists 13 open actions with proposed owners (the team confirms), deadlines and source ids.

Brief status (r3): the VTC brief, site plans and 3D model have never been opened. S01 does not state tower heights, FSR, jury weights, boards or file size; those come from the project description (S78). Open the brief before registration closes on 29 Oct (A1); until then brief-derived items are hypotheses.

Key facts (21 Oct 2026): registration closes 29 Oct, Q&A 3 Nov, submission 30 Nov 23:59 London (40 days); teams up to 4; fee EUR 120 or 140 plus 4.5% VAT (mapping inferred); prizes CAD 15,000 incl. Student and Sustainability Awards of CAD 1,000 (a top-3 entry wins both). Policy context: the current Higher Buildings Policy area may consider up to 600 ft (183 m) (S75), below the 244-305 m in S78; the competition will not set policy.

What a student team can get before 30 Nov: Forma free (vendor statement; confirm logged in); Snaptrude Student Plan free; Rhino USD 195 student or a 30-user lab licence at USD 975 if UBC buys; Ladybug free; Eddy3D free, OpenFOAM, Rhino 8.27 (plugin licence unnamed); Speckle Explore plus academic workspace (terms unknown); Giraffe free (vendor statement); Infrared Free 900 tokens (42 days); Finch free single-user tier; EC3 free; ShapeDiver 14-day trial or academic (non-commercial). SimScale: no free urban-wind route (LBM and PWC excluded on Community, Free Academic and Sponsorship). Not available: cove analysis.tool. Unknown: TestFit class terms, Hypar, Archistar, UpCodes.

Competition-use status (none confirmed in writing): Forma unread (403); Snaptrude educational use only; ShapeDiver non-commercial only; Giraffe EULA silent; Speckle no terms; SimScale Sponsorship aimed at competition teams; Infrared not stated; Eddy3D free for all users stated; Rhino buy page states no restriction (EULA unread).

Design lessons for the tool: (1) no commercial tool opened exposes sourced thresholds, so they are benchmarks, not dependencies; (2) open, scriptable options are Ladybug Tools (AGPL-3.0; Butterfly GPL-3.0+), Eddy3D (OpenFOAM), Speckle (Apache-2.0) and Hypar Elements/HyparSpace (MIT); the platform licence and deployment boundary go to the DATA packet because AGPL section 13 attaches to modified versions offered over a network; (3) the course demos give three module patterns: B (checker script, hook, reviewer), C (scorer, front file, rounds, cap in code, per-family helpers) and D (constraints reader that flags contradictions before design, analyst that reports only measured numbers); each shows a guard covers only the path it watches; (4) code, AI and people are separated per step: code results are measurements, LLM helpers vary run to run (demo D), and people decide criteria, interpretation of City in Nature and reconciliation, which guideline to breach, and any engagement with the Nations; (5) protected views point to the Public Views Guidelines (2024), whose heights a person must read from the PDF (403); the 24 City polygons are the verified starting point and six approximate downtown sample points each fall in at least one cone; (6) cloud tools may expose the entry before anonymous judging.

As-is evidence: every step is a HYPOTHESIS (interview n=0). Two 15-minute interviews are planned by 5 Nov (A12); until recorded, the step ranking must not drive module priority.
